title: PVANet: Lightweight Deep Neural Networks for Real-time Object Detection

problem.summary: Even the best modern object detectors remain too computationally expensive for practical real-time use, and the paper argues existing network architectures are highly redundant, so redundancy should be removed at the design stage rather than only via post-hoc compression.
statements: Detection speed is limited by heavy computational cost even when accuracy is already acceptable for commercial use.
Modern CNN architectures contain large amounts of redundancy that inflate compute requirements.
Compression and quantization help but do not remove redundancy introduced by the network architecture itself.

evidence.quote: However, in terms of detection speed, even the best algorithms are still suffering from heavy computational cost.
The successes in network compression [1] and decomposition of convolution kernels [2, 3] imply that present network architectures are highly redundant.
it is still important to reduce the computational cost in the network design stage.

background.summary: PVANet keeps the Faster R-CNN detection framework and reuses recent efficiency-building blocks (C.ReLU, Inception, batch normalization, residual connections), claiming that no prior work combined them into a thin-but-deep detector.

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: detection framework that PVANet follows with modifications
relatedWork.quote: We basically follow the method of Faster R-CNN[11], but we introduce some modifications specialized for object detection.

relatedWork.name: C.ReLU
relatedWork.relation: adopted in early layers and modified with a separated bias layer
relatedWork.quote: C.ReLU can double the number of output channels by simply concatenating negated outputs before applying ReLU.

relatedWork.name: Inception
relatedWork.relation: adopted in later layers as a cost-effective multi-scale block
relatedWork.quote: We have found that Inception can be one of the most cost-effective building blocks for capturing both small and large objects in an input image.

relatedWork.name: ResNet / batch normalization
relatedWork.relation: training techniques used to make the deep thin network trainable
relatedWork.quote: adopting residual structures with pre-activation [10] and batch normalization [7]

evidence.quote: Therefore, reducing these redundancies is a straightforward approach in reducing the computational cost.
Although recent reports on network compression and quantization shows promising results, it is still important to reduce the computational cost in the network design stage.

solution.summary: PVANet is a lightweight feature extractor following the principle of more layers with fewer channels, using modified C.ReLU in early stages and Inception blocks later, with multi-scale hyper-feature concatenation feeding a Faster R-CNN detection head.
solution.approach: Design a thin-but-deep VGG-style backbone (mCReLU + Inception + residuals) and concatenate multi-scale features into a lightweight RPN/classifier pipeline.
components: Modified C.ReLU (mCReLU) with a separated bias layer
Inception blocks where a 5x5 convolution is replaced by two 3x3 convolutions
Hyper-feature concatenation of 1/4, 1/16 and 1/32 scale layers fused by a 1x1x512 convolution
RPN fed only the first 128 channels of convf to save 1.4 GMAC
RPN with 42 anchors across 6 scales and 7 aspect ratios
Plateau-detection learning rate scheduling with batch normalization and residual connections

evidence.quote: Based on the basic principle of “smaller number of output channels with more layers”, we adopt C.ReLU[4] in the initial layers and Inception structure[5] in the latter part of the network.

Combining fine-grained details with highly abstracted information in the feature extraction layer helps the following region proposal network and classification network detect objects of different scales.
our RPN uses 42 anchors of 6 scales (32, 48, 80, 144, 256, 512) and 7 aspect ratios (0.333, 0.5, 0.667, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0).

experiments.summary: PVANet is pre-trained on ImageNet 2012 and evaluated on the PASCAL VOC2007/VOC2012 detection tasks against Faster R-CNN, R-FCN and SSD variants, reporting mAP, recall, runtime and compute cost (GMAC).

evidence.quote: 84.9% and 84.2%mAP on VOC2007 and VOC2012 while the required compute is less than 10% of the recent ResNet-101.
The overall detection accuracy of plain PVAN ET in VOC2007 reaches 84.4% mean AP.
Our PVAN ET + has achieved the 4th place on the leaderboard as of the time of submission, and the network shows 84.2% mAP

limitations.summary: Evaluation covers only ImageNet classification and PASCAL VOC detection (no COCO), the fastest configuration trades a small accuracy drop for speed, and headline speed numbers depend on a single high-end GPU setup.
items: No results on the COCO detection benchmark are reported; experiments are limited to ImageNet 2012, VOC2007 and VOC2012.
Compressing the fully-connected layers for speed costs 0.5% mAP.
Runtime comparisons against competitors are estimated/projected rather than measured under one identical setup.

evidence.quote: we present experimental results on ImageNet 2012 classification, VOC-2007 and VOC-2012 benchmarks with detailed training and testing methodologies (Section 3).
the compressed network can run in 31.3 FPS with only 0.5% accuracy drop.
while we projected the original values with an assumption that NVIDIA Titan X is 1.5x faster than NVIDIA K40.

futureDirections.direction: Apply the thin-but-deep design principle to other vision tasks such as face recognition and semantic analysis.
futureDirections.quote: we believe that our design principle is widely applicable to other tasks such as face recognition and semantic analysis.

futureDirections.direction: Combine the architecture with network compression and quantization techniques for further real-world speedups.
futureDirections.quote: All kinds of recent compression and quantization techniques are applicable to our network as well to further increase the actual performance in real applications.

futureDirections.direction: Integrate complementary efficient detection structures (R-FCN, SSD) with PVANet.
futureDirections.quote: their methodologies can be easily integrated with PVAN ET and further reduce its computational cost.

applications.detail: The introduction positions the work as enabling commercialization of detection in automotive and surveillance markets.
applications.quote: accuracies acceptable for commercialization in a broad range of markets like automotive and surveillance.

applications.detail: The compressed variant reaches 31.3 FPS, targeting real-time operation on desktop-class hardware.
applications.quote: the compressed network can run in 31.3 FPS with only 0.5% accuracy drop.

deploymentClaims: Less than 10% of the compute required by ResNet-101 while reaching 84.9% and 84.2% mAP on VOC2007/VOC2012.
PVANet+ runs in 46 ms (21.7 FPS) on an NVIDIA Titan X; the compressed model runs at 31.3 FPS.
Among networks over 80% mAP on the VOC2012 leaderboard, PVANet+ is the only one running in <= 50 ms.
Code and trained models are released publicly at github.com/sanghoon/pva-faster-rcnn.

evidence.quote: Among the networks performing over 80% mAP, PVAN ET + is the only network running in ≤ 50ms.
All evaluations were done on Intel i7-6700K CPU with a single core and NVIDIA Titan X GPU.
